rollups.text: The user was creating the constructed language Flang and discussing its grammar on 2023-06-02. The possessive/genitive ending is -i and the possessor precedes the possessed noun: flom (“dog”) becomes flomi, and fash (“house”) becomes fashi; “the dog’s house” is “Flomi fash,” while “the house’s dog” is “Fashi flom.” The definite article is fi and the indefinite article fa, both before nouns. Nouns were described with accusative -a, genitive -i, and instrumental -u; the assistant also supplied corresponding verb-form examples. The assistant gave “Fi flom fika fa fol” for “The dog eats a cat,” and “Fi flom fiko fa fol” and “Fi fona fiko fa fol” for the past-tense sentences “The dog ate a cat” and “The woman ate a cat.” The recorded discussion establishes these examples but no later development or complete grammar.

The assistant gave conflicting food-supply estimates—about 43–45 days in one calculation and about 24 days total, with 14 days remaining after 10 days, in another—based on assumptions not measured by the user. No app choice or actual tracking results are recorded.
